rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Scarlet fever is caused by group A streptococci and is a notifiable disease in England and Wales.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Schools and nurseries should contact their health protection team when an outbreak is suspected or defined.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Children and staff who are ill should stay away from the setting until they are well enough to return.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: A diagnosed case should remain away from school, nursery or work for at least 24 hours after starting antibiotics.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Frequent handwashing and respiratory hygiene help reduce transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Settings should clean frequently touched surfaces and contaminated shared items during outbreaks.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Cuts, grazes and wounds should be cleaned and covered to reduce routes for invasive infection.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Outbreak response may include parent communication, case finding and enhanced environmental cleaning.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Scarlet-fever risk depends on case timing, contact patterns, setting, hygiene, vulnerability, treatment and outbreak response.

rows.source: UKHSA scarlet fever and Group A Strep outbreak controls
rows.verified: Scarlet-fever evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, treatment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis A is an infectious disease that affects the liver.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: The virus is present in the faeces of an infected person and can spread through contaminated hands, food and surfaces.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Good hand hygiene is a primary control for preventing person-to-person spread.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Vaccination is an important preventive measure for people at increased risk.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Post-exposure public-health management may include vaccination or immunoglobulin according to risk and timing.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Symptoms can include fever, flu-like illness, nausea and jaundice.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Most people recover, but severe liver disease can occur in rare cases.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Public-health guidance supports case assessment, contact management and outbreak control.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis-A risk depends on immunity, exposure route, hygiene, contact timing, food handling, vulnerability and prophylaxis.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis-A evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, vaccination- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
